post.text:
hey jude was written for john lennon's son
.
.
.
John was leaving his wife Cynthia. Paul drove out to see her and their five-year-old son Julian, and started writing a song to comfort him. It started as Hey Jules. Paul changed the name to Jude because it was easier to sing.

At more than seven minutes, it was one of the longest singles ever released at the time. Hey Jude spent nine weeks at #1 in the US, the longest run of any Beatles single.

Best Beatles song? Follow @vinylduel for a music story every day.

post.text:
he released his last album two days before he died
.
.
.
David Bowie had been treated for cancer for about 18 months, and kept it almost completely private. His album Blackstar came out on 8 January 2016, his 69th birthday. Fans heard it as a bold new chapter.

He died two days later. Songs like Lazarus suddenly sounded like a goodbye, and producer Tony Visconti called the album his parting gift. His first big hit, Space Oddity, came out days before the Apollo 11 launch, and the BBC played it during its moon-landing coverage.

post.text:
5 old songs that tv and tiktok brought back 🎧

1. Running Up That Hill: Stranger Things made the 1985 song a UK #1 in 2022.
2. Master of Puppets: Eddie's guitar solo in Stranger Things sent the 1986 song onto the Billboard Hot 100 for the first time.
3. Dreams: A 2020 TikTok of a man skateboarding with a bottle of cranberry juice sent Dreams back onto the charts, 43 years later.
4. Bohemian Rhapsody: The head-banging car scene in Wayne's World (1992) took it back up the US charts, to #2.
5. Saltburn: Sophie Ellis-Bextor's 2001 hit returned to the charts after the film's final scene.

Which song needs a comeback? Follow @vinylduel for a music story every day.

.

On VinylDuel you rank an album by picking between two songs, again and again, until the whole order is worked out. Most duels are easy. These ones aren't.

The community can barely separate Money and Time on The Dark Side of the Moon. Runaway and Power are exactly tied on My Beautiful Dark Twisted Fantasy, and so are R U Mine? and Why'd You Only Call Me When You're High? on AM. Let It Happen just beats New Person, Same Old Mistakes, and Just just beats Fake Plastic Trees.

to pimp a butterfly: rap's great jazz record 🎧

Our take. Jazz, funk and spoken word, with Thundercat, Kamasi Washington and George Clinton. A dense album about race, fame and self-worth. Alright became a protest anthem, and King Kunta still knocks. It's long and demanding: an album you study, not one you put on in the background.

Verdict: 9.5/10. A modern classic.

post.text:
the black parade turns 20
.
.
.
Our take. A concept album about a dying man called The Patient, framed as a marching band's parade. Huge, theatrical, and unlike anything around it. Welcome to the Black Parade is still a perfect rock song, and Famous Last Words is still the ending everyone screams along to. The story gets lost in the middle, and a couple of songs feel more like costume than feeling.

Verdict: 9.0/10. Still the best emo album ever made.

5 songs you didn't know were covers 🎧

1. Hurt: Johnny Cash's most famous late song was first recorded by Nine Inch Nails in 1994.
2. Nothing Compares 2 U: Sinéad O'Connor's 1990 hit was written by Prince years earlier, for a side project.
3. I Will Always Love You: Whitney Houston's 1992 smash was written and first recorded by Dolly Parton in the 1970s.
4. Respect: Otis Redding released Respect in 1965. Aretha Franklin's 1967 version made it an anthem.
5. Tainted Love: Soft Cell's 1981 hit was a cover of a 1964 soul song by Gloria Jones.

Which one surprised you? Follow @vinylduel for a music story every day.

post.text:
5 hits that other artists turned down
.
.
.
1. Hit 01: Her team passed. Rihanna's 2007 version spent ten weeks at #1 in the UK.
2. Hit 02: Kylie said no. Britney Spears recorded it and won her first Grammy for it.
3. Hit 03: His label passed, so Pharrell recorded it himself. It became one of the biggest songs of 2014.
4. Hit 04: TLC passed. It became Britney Spears' debut single and a #1 around the world.
5. Hit 05: His label felt it wasn't right for him. Leona Lewis made it a worldwide #1.

Which one would you have kept? Follow @vinylduel for a music story every day.
